exposure: Uterine artery ligation (to induce Intrauterine Growth Retardation - IUGR)
outcome: Density and proportion of NeuN-positive cells
cohort: Rat fetuses obtained from pregnant rats, with some undergoing uterine artery ligation to induce growth retardation and others serving as controls from the untied uterine horn.
finding: Intrauterine growth retardation (IUGR) did not affect cell proliferation in the subventricular zone, but it reduced neuronal survival in the cerebral parietal cortex, associated with a decrease in pERK-positive cell density and proportion.
gest_age: Fetuses were obtained at 21 days of gestation; uterine artery ligation was performed at 17 days of gestation.
